lines.li: [us] What will your stone build?
[them,their:tribal] Houses for the cold moons, and a hearth for each.
[them] Somebody's wall, somebody's hearth, a bridge if the price is right.
[us] Nothing for yourselves?
[them] A stonecutter's house is always the last one finished.
[them] Wet stone fights the chisel.
[us] Will you stop for the rain?
[them] Only when it fights back harder than I do.
[us] How many beasts have you shorn this year?
[them] Enough that I count them in my sleep.
[us] Does it get easier?
[them] The beasts don't, but the hands do.
[them] Good wool grows on a calm beast.
[us] Ours are calm enough.
[them] They'll be calmer still out of those heavy coats.
[us] What happens to the ones you catch?
[them] We gentle them and sell them to farms that want a beast that knows the land.
[us] Do they ever go back to the wild?
[them] The clever ones try.
[them,their:tribal] We call a few out of the herd, and we never take the mothers.
[them] We take a few from the herd, and never the mothers.
[us] Why not the mothers?
[them] Then there would be no herd next year.
[us] What do you teach them?
[them,their:tribal] The old tellings, and how to count the moons.
[them,their:spacer] Reading, figures, and how to check what a machine tells you.
[them] Letters, numbers, and how to ask a good question.
[us] Which is the hardest?
[them] The question, every time.
[them] Every settlement has a child who asks the one question I can't answer.
[us] What do you tell them?
[them] That I'll know by the next time I come.
[us] How is the wound?
[them] Healing, slower than I'd like.
[us] Rest here as long as you need.
[them] A few more days, then home.
[us] Was it a hard fight?
[them] Every fight is hard when you're in it.
[us] Will you go back to it?
[them] Not if I can help it.
[them] You're the one who knows medicine here?
[us] I am, how is it holding up?
[them] Clean, at least, which is more than I hoped for.
